verdict.probe_answer: The memo lands on the vindicated design: a span-keyed class_bases: BTreeMap<(file, class_span), Vec<String>> map on CallGraph, populated at all build sites, with a conservative policy — resolve only on a single unambiguous provider, treat external/ambiguous/multi-branch bases as barriers (drop, don't guess), and an explicit, well-argued case that full Python C3 is unnecessary. This is exactly the shape that shipped (498482a / 1df081d / 2fb6457). It also correctly rejects the naive bare-name owner_lookup trap, citing 1a's own collision fix as the reason to stay span-keyed. Its one gap versus the final scope: the memo recurses up an arbitrarily-deep same-file single-inheritance chain, whereas the shipped spec was narrowed further to a single DEPTH-1 direct-base hop only ('sound by simplification') — a refinement the memo didn't anticipate, though its own data (13/13 real hits were direct/depth-1) already supported that narrower cut.
verdict.rationale: Core design elements — span-keyed identity, all-build-site population, single-unambiguous-provider/barrier semantics, and the no-C3-needed argument — match the settled outcome closely enough that following this memo would have anchored the team at essentially the final architecture, sidestepping most of the churn implied by the 4 spec REWORKs. The only miscalibration is scope depth (chain-walk vs. depth-1-only), a minor overshoot within the same conservative design family rather than a different approach, so it doesn't change the overall verdict.
